_about: Grounded evidence for the ADR-009 cost RATES (PricingRates + compute discount lever). Each rate was researched from real vendor/aggregator pricing pages and then attacked by 3 independent devil's-advocate verifiers (lenses: citation-resolution / unit-region-SKU / cherry-pick-band), each of which re-fetched the cited URLs. Values are integer engine units (micro-USD per the rate's unit; basis points RETAINED for discounts). This file is the durable record — AI proposed, a human (Bifola) RATIFIED the citations (#71 merged on "ratify #71"). Region/SKU scope is US-East / standard tiers. measured_date 2026-06-23. Wired into the report via `grounding.ground_pricing` (ADR-009 slice 2): the PricingRates seed values mirror the `engine_value` central here, and the report shows the rates as GROUNDED when grounding is active (KB_PROVIDER=curated; the default stub renders them unchanged).
verification_method: research + 3x adversarial verification (devil's-advocate, refute-by-default); citations independently re-fetched; load-bearing rates spot-checked again by the lead before encoding

rates.context_note: US region (us-east-1/equiv) standard internet data-transfer-OUT, first paid tier after the 100GB/mo free tier, ~1-10TB/mo band. Central 0.09 = AWS rate; band spans Azure 0.087 to GCP Premium-default 0.12.
rates.caveat: Strict 1-10TB GCP Premium is 0.11; 0.12 is GCP's 0-1TB entry sub-tier (every workload's first TB bills at 0.12 on default Premium). Rate steps DOWN above 10TB (AWS 0.085 / Azure 0.083 / GCP 0.08). Non-US regions cost materially more (Sao Paulo ~0.15). Inter-region/CDN/peering egress are separate SKUs, out of scope.

citations.conditions: Premium tier default, US source region

rates.adversarial_summary: 3/3 confirmed. Every cited URL re-fetched and contained its number; rates independently corroborated by search. Only finding: the 0.12 band-high is GCP's 0-1TB entry rate (vs 0.11 strict 1-10TB) — disclosed, legitimate as a real-workload ceiling. Band clears the T2 floor.

rates.context_note: Object storage STANDARD/hot tier, US-East single-region/LRS, first paid tier (first 50TB/mo). Storage only. Per-provider: AWS S3 0.023, Azure Blob Hot 0.018, GCS 0.020-0.022. Central 0.021 ~ four-point mean.
rates.caveat: Headline per-GB is a small slice of real object-storage spend once requests/retrieval/egress are added. Rates tier down above 50TB; geo-redundant ~2x. Band high 0.0253 = GCP us-east4 (N. Virginia) equivalent.

citations.conditions: Block Blob Hot, LRS, East US

rates.adversarial_summary: 3/3 confirmed; all 4 URLs re-fetched verbatim. Minor: a one-month Finout date typo, a GCS 0.020-vs-0.022 split (both in band). Band widened high to 0.0253 (GCP N. Virginia) to honestly span the spread and clear the T2 floor (~17.4%).

Re-verify LLM prices quarterly.

rates.context_note: 1-year commitment, NO-UPFRONT, general-purpose Linux compute, US, % off on-demand. Central 30% off (7000 bp retained) = conservative flexible cross-provider anchor (AWS Compute SP, GCP Compute Flexible CUD 28%). Resource-locked operating point ~37-42% off is the band's upper end.
rates.caveat: No vendor publishes a clean '1yr no-upfront %' table. AWS's 30%/40% example is explicitly hypothetical AND partial-upfront. CORRECTS THE SEED DOWN: the old 40% off (6000 bp) was optimistic; realistic 1yr general-purpose is ~36-37% off (resource-locked) and ~28-30% (flexible). Vendor 'up to 55/72%' headlines are 3yr/all-upfront/memory-optimized maxima.

citations.quoted: Compute SP 30%, EC2 Instance SP 40% (1yr partial-upfront, labelled hypothetical)

rates.adversarial_summary: 2/3 — the cherry-pick verifier correctly refuted the original 55% top edge (it conflated 3yr/memory-optimized maxima). Independent search confirmed realistic 1yr general-purpose ~36-37% off. High edge lowered 55%->42% off. 30% off is the conservative cross-provider central.

rates.context_note: 3-year compute commitment, standard general-purpose VM, US-East, All-Upfront, % off on-demand. Central 55% off (4500 bp retained) is a conservative cross-provider blend (AWS vendor 3yr 60%; Usage.ai m5.large 65%; GCP general-purpose flexible CUD 46% sets the floor). 72% ceiling is a SKU-specific marketing maximum.
rates.caveat: Varies by commitment product (AWS Standard RI vs GCP flexible vs resource-based CUD vs Azure RI), VM family, region, OS, payment. 55% off ~ correction up from the old 60% off seed toward the conservative cross-provider blend (GCP general-purpose is only 46% off). 72% off achievable only for specific high-end SKUs with max payment. Watch: MS retires older Azure RI SKUs from 2026-07-01.

citations.conditions: Standard RI — re-confirmed first-party by the lead

citations.quoted: up to 72% vs PAYG (1 or 3 yr)

rates.adversarial_summary: 3/3 confirmed, no value change. AWS vendor (60%/up-to-72%), GCP (46% flexible), ProsperOps (Azure up-to-72%), Usage.ai (m5.large 65%) all re-fetched verbatim. 72% is used as band ceiling only (not central); 55% is conservative vs the AWS/Azure ~60-62% cluster; floor 46% = GCP verified general-purpose. ~24% half-width, clears T1.

rates.context_note: Spot/preemptible/interruptible compute discount, % off on-demand. Vendor ceilings: AWS/Azure 'up to 90%', GCP 'up to 91%' with explicit 60% contractual floor. Central 77% off (2300 bp retained) reflects the consensus pull below the marketing ceiling; band 55-91% captures the documented sub-60% tail (Azure VMSS 53-76%).
rates.caveat: Do NOT default to 90% — that's a best-case ceiling. Realistic operating point is workload-dependent across 55-91%: standalone CPU spot clusters high (86-88%), VMSS / GPU-in-constrained-region / Graviton pull down with a fat left tail below 60%. CORRECTS THE SEED DOWN from 80% off. Spot capacity is non-guaranteed (eviction: Azure 30s, AWS 2min) — treat any spot saving as conditional, not contractual.

citations.quoted: between 60% and 91% off; floor at least 60%
citations.conditions: Spot VMs; may change up to monthly

citations.quoted: up to 90%; typically 86-88% standalone, 53-76% in VMSS

rates.adversarial_summary: 2/3 — the cherry-pick verifier refuted 80% as too optimistic, and BOTH confirming verifiers conceded the point (measured AWS 67-80%, GCP midpoint 75.5%, Azure VMSS below 60%). Central reconciled DOWN to 77%, floor lowered to 55% to absorb the documented left tail. All 6 citations re-fetched, zero invented.
